questions.q: Which group of hormones acts through intracellular receptors and is transported in plasma bound to carrier proteins?

options.e: Wrong. These are hydrophilic, use plasma-membrane receptors and need no transport proteins.
Wrong. Catecholamines are hydrophilic and act on cell surface receptors.
Wrong. They act through cell surface tyrosine kinase cascades.

options.t: Steroids, thyroid hormones, calcitriol and retinoids (Group I)
options.e: Correct. Lipophilic Group I hormones use intracellular receptors, travel on transport proteins and have long half-lives.

questions.q: Which feature is found only in Group II hormones and not in Group I hormones?

options.e: Wrong. Both groups can alter gene transcription.

options.t: Plasma half-life of hours to days
options.e: Wrong. Long half-life is a Group I feature.
Wrong. This is the Group I mediator.

options.t: Effects including protein translocation and protein modification
options.e: Correct. Both groups affect gene transcription, transporters and channels; only Group II also cause protein translocation and modification.

questions.q: Which hormone acts through the cAMP second messenger system?

options.e: Wrong. ANP uses cGMP.
Wrong. Angiotensin II uses the calcium/phosphatidylinositol system.
Correct. Glucagon, ACTH, FSH, LH, TSH, PTH, calcitonin and renal V2 ADH use Gs, adenylyl cyclase and cAMP.
Wrong. Insulin uses a tyrosine kinase cascade.

questions.q: After a hormone binds a Gs-coupled receptor, what happens first at the G protein?

options.t: GTP on the alpha subunit is hydrolyzed to GDP
options.e: Wrong. GTP hydrolysis switches the G protein off.

options.t: Adenylyl cyclase converts ATP to cAMP
options.e: Wrong. This happens after alpha-GTP dissociates and activates the enzyme.

options.t: Protein kinase A releases its catalytic subunits
options.e: Wrong. This follows the rise in cAMP.

options.t: GDP on the alpha subunit is replaced by GTP
options.e: Correct. The receptor conformational change is followed by GDP-GTP exchange on the alpha subunit.

questions.q: How does cAMP activate protein kinase A?

options.t: It binds the catalytic subunits and phosphorylates them
options.e: Wrong. cAMP binds the regulatory subunits.

options.t: It binds the regulatory subunits, releasing two active catalytic subunits
options.e: Correct. The freed catalytic subunits phosphorylate substrates using phosphate from ATP.

options.t: It phosphorylates the regulatory subunits directly
options.e: Wrong. cAMP is an allosteric activator, not a kinase.

options.t: It binds the receptor and activates adenylyl cyclase
options.e: Wrong. cAMP is made by adenylyl cyclase, not an activator of it.

questions.q: Which enzyme degrades cAMP to AMP and thereby helps terminate the signal?

options.e: Wrong. Phosphatase removes phosphate from the protein substrate.
Correct. Phosphodiesterase breaks cAMP into AMP.
Wrong. This enzyme makes cAMP from ATP.
Wrong. This enzyme makes cGMP from GTP.

questions.q: Which property of the G protein alpha subunit allows it to switch itself off?

options.e: Wrong. Adenylyl cyclase is a separate effector enzyme.
Wrong. This is a feature of the insulin receptor beta chain.
Wrong. Phosphodiesterase is a separate enzyme.
Correct. It hydrolyzes GTP to GDP and then rebinds the beta-gamma subunits.

questions.q: Phospholipase C cleaves PIP2 into which two second messengers?

options.e: Correct. PIP2 (phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate) yields diacylglycerol and inositol trisphosphate.
Wrong. cAMP is made by adenylyl cyclase, and PKA is a kinase.
Wrong. PKC is a kinase and NO acts via cGMP.
Wrong. cGMP is made by guanylate cyclase from GTP.

questions.q: Where does IP3 bind to cause release of calcium?

options.t: Its receptor on the plasma membrane
options.e: Wrong. IP3 is a soluble messenger acting inside the cell.

options.t: The regulatory subunit of protein kinase A
options.e: Wrong. That site binds cAMP.

options.t: Its receptor on the endoplasmic reticulum
options.e: Correct. IP3 binding on the ER releases Ca2+ into the cytosol.
Wrong. That binds insulin.

questions.q: Which combination synergistically activates protein kinase C?

options.e: Correct. The C in PKC reflects calcium dependence.
Wrong. cAMP activates protein kinase A.
Wrong. IP3 releases calcium; cGMP acts via protein kinase G.
Wrong. cAMP does not activate protein kinase C.

questions.q: Which hormone acts through the phosphatidylinositol/calcium system?

options.e: Wrong. ACTH uses cAMP.
Correct. Muscarinic ACh, alpha-1 catecholamines, angiotensin II and extra-renal V1 ADH use this pathway.
Wrong. PTH uses cAMP.
Wrong. Erythropoietin uses a tyrosine kinase cascade.

questions.q: Which pairing of vasopressin receptors and effects is correct?

options.t: V1: cAMP, antidiuresis; V2: phosphatidylinositol/calcium, vasoconstriction
options.e: Wrong. This reverses the pairing.

options.t: V1: phosphatidylinositol/calcium, vasoconstriction; V2: cAMP, antidiuresis
options.e: Correct. V2 in the kidney acts via adenylyl cyclase and cAMP.

options.t: V1: cGMP, vasodilatation; V2: cAMP, antidiuresis
options.e: Wrong. V1 does not use cGMP.

options.t: V1: tyrosine kinase, growth; V2: phosphatidylinositol, antidiuresis
options.e: Wrong. Neither receptor uses a tyrosine kinase cascade.

questions.q: Which hormone's receptor directly activates guanylate cyclase to convert GTP to cGMP?

options.e: Wrong. Glucagon uses cAMP.
Wrong. GH uses a tyrosine kinase cascade.
Wrong. V1 uses phospholipase C.
Correct. The ANP receptor itself has guanylate cyclase activity.

questions.q: Which part of the insulin receptor forms the insulin binding site?

options.e: Wrong. The beta chain spans the membrane and carries the tyrosine kinase domain.
Correct. The alpha chains are extracellular and bind insulin.
Wrong. Alpha chains are extracellular.
Wrong. The insulin receptor is not G-protein coupled.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of events after insulin binds its receptor?

options.t: IRS phosphorylation, beta autophosphorylation, conformational change, kinase activation
options.e: Wrong. IRS phosphorylation follows autophosphorylation.

options.t: GDP/GTP exchange, adenylyl cyclase activation, cAMP rise, PKA activation
options.e: Wrong. This is the cAMP pathway, not insulin signaling.

options.t: Conformational change, beta autophosphorylation, IRS phosphorylation, kinase activation
options.e: Correct. Tyrosine autophosphorylation precedes phosphorylation of IRS proteins.

options.t: PIP2 cleavage, IP3 release, calcium rise, PKC activation
options.e: Wrong. This is the phosphatidylinositol pathway.

questions.q: Which statement correctly pairs an embryonic signaling factor with its receptor system?

options.t: TGF-beta/Nodal: serine/threonine kinase receptors acting through Smad
options.e: Correct. These control left-right axis, dorsal-ventral patterning and gastrulation.

options.t: FGF: serine/threonine kinase receptors acting through Smad
options.e: Wrong. FGFs signal through receptor tyrosine kinases and MAPK.

options.t: hCG: receptor tyrosine kinase acting through MAPK
options.e: Wrong. hCG acts through a GPCR and cAMP/PKA.
Wrong. IGFs use RTK with PI3K/Akt; GH and prolactin use JAK/STAT.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly describes the Ras/MAPK branch of FGF receptor signaling?

options.t: GRB2, SOS, RAS, RAF, MAPKK, MAPK, AP-1
options.e: Correct. RAS is converted from GDP-bound to GTP-bound form, ending with the transcription factor AP-1.

options.t: PI3K, PDK, AKT, TSC1/2, RHEB, mTOR
options.e: Wrong. This is the PI3K/Akt branch.
Wrong. This is the cAMP pathway.
Wrong. This is the phosphatidylinositol pathway.

questions.q: Which protein opposes the PI3K/Akt branch by reversing PIP2 to PIP3 conversion?

options.e: Wrong. RAF belongs to the Ras/MAPK branch.
Wrong. RHEB activates mTOR downstream of Akt.
Correct. PTEN opposes this branch.
Wrong. SOS activates RAS in the MAPK branch.

questions.q: Which hypothalamic hormone is a cyclic peptide that inhibits GH and TSH?

options.e: Correct. It is a 14-amino-acid cyclic peptide inhibiting GH, TSH and gut, pancreatic and gastric secretion.
Wrong. TRH is a tripeptide that stimulates TSH and prolactin.
Wrong. GnRH is a decapeptide releasing LH and FSH.
Wrong. GHRH stimulates GH secretion.

questions.q: Which hormone acts through a tyrosine kinase cascade rather than a G protein?

options.e: Wrong. TSH uses Gs and cAMP.
Wrong. Calcitonin uses cAMP.
Correct. Insulin, GH, prolactin and erythropoietin use receptor tyrosine kinase cascades.
Wrong. It uses the phosphatidylinositol/calcium system.
